title: Cocoa-Dusted Dark Chocolate Truffles
summary: Rich, melt-in-the-mouth dark chocolate truffles made from a simple two-ingredient ganache and rolled in cocoa.
equipment: 20 cm square dish lined with baking paper

ingredients.note: check the label; many contain soya lecithin or traces of milk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the coating
steps.text: Sift the cocoa and icing sugar together onto a shallow plate. A touch of sugar softens the bitterness of the cocoa without making the coating sweet.

steps.title: Make the ganache
steps.text: Tip the chopped chocolate and salt into the heatproof bowl. Bring the cream just to a simmer, pour it over, leave for 2 min, then stir from the middle outwards until the mixture is smooth and shiny. Chopping the chocolate finely means it melts evenly without lumps.

steps.title: Let it set
steps.text: Scrape the ganache into the lined dish and refrigerate for about 45 min, until it is firm enough to hold a scoop.

steps.title: Portion
steps.text: Scoop out 24 heaped teaspoons and set them on a plate. Chill for 30 min more so they are easy to handle.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Working quickly with cool hands (or gloves), roll each portion into a rough ball. They do not need to be perfect; real truffles are a little irregular.

steps.title: Coat and chill
steps.text: Roll the balls in the cocoa mixture, shake off any excess and refrigerate for 30 min. Take them out 10 min before serving so the centres soften.

tips: A common mistake is overheating the cream; a hard boil can make the ganache split and look greasy, so stop at a gentle simmer.
If your hands are warm, run them under cold water and dry well before rolling.
Use chocolate of about 60% cocoa; much darker chocolate needs a little extra cream to stay soft.
Roll in chopped toasted nuts instead of cocoa for a different finish.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 week, with a little extra cocoa to stop them sticking. Serve after 10 min at room temperature.
